High Availability/Load Balancing – Ability to live-migrate a VM to other physical server
Rapid provisioning – On demand provisioning of hardware resources
Encapsulation – The execution environment of an application is encapsulated within VM
Lower Costs – Increased Efficiencies, flexibility and responsiveness

edits.title: x86 Ring Privilege Levels
bullets: Observation 1: Only Ring 0 can invoke privileged instructions; Rings 1, 2, and 3 trap when invoking privileged instructions.
Observation 2: An x86 PTE has a single bit to indicate user/supervisor, and the MMU maps Rings 0‑2 to “supervisor” and Ring 3 to “user.”
The Normal x86 Setup.

“Isolated” drivers in Rings 1 or 2 can still access Ring 0 memory pages, so isolation is weak in practice without additional segment‑based protection (segment support was dropped in x86‑64).
Most non‑x86 chips define only two privilege levels, so portable OSes shouldn’t rely on Rings 1 and 2 for privileged operations.

edits.title: Kubernetes (also know as K8s) Basics
bullets: Kubernetes as seen earlier is a container or microservice platform that orchestrates computing, networking, and storage infrastructure workloads. Kubernetes extends how we scale containerized applications so that we can enjoy all the benefits of a truly immutable infrastructure.
Pod: a group of one or more containers.
ReplicaSet (RS): ensures the desired number of pods is running.
Deployment: offers declarative updates for pods in a ReplicaSet.
StatefulSet: a workload API object that manages stateful applications such as databases.
DaemonSet: ensures all or some worker nodes run a copy of a pod; useful for daemon applications like Fluentd.
Job: creates one or more pods, runs a task to completion, then deletes the pod(s).
Service: an abstraction that defines a logical set of pods, the policy, and an endpoint for accessing them.
Volume: an abstraction that lets us persist data because containers are ephemeral and data is deleted when the container is deleted.
Namespace: a segment of the cluster dedicated to a certain purpose (e.g., project or team), used to create multiple virtual Kubernetes clusters within a single cluster.

edits.title: Kubernetes Architecture
bullets: A K8S cluster is made of a Master node, which exposes the API, schedules deployments, and generally manages the cluster. This is the entry point of all administrative tasks. The master node orchestrates the worker nodes where services run.
Worker nodes (multiple of them) can be responsible for container runtime, like Docker.
Kube-apiserver exposes the API as the entry point for all REST commands used to control the cluster.
etcd is a key‑value store for all cluster data, used for shared configuration and service discovery, including jobs, pod/service details, state, namespaces and replication information.
Kube-scheduler has information on available resources and schedules new pods on worker nodes.
Kube-controller-manager runs the controllers, uses the apiserver to watch the shared cluster state and makes corrective changes to reach the desired state.
The Replication controller takes care of the number of pods in the system as configured by the user.
edits.source_text:
Kubernetes Architecture
A K8S cluster is made of a
Master node, which exposes the API, schedules deployments, and generally manages the cluster. This is the entry point of all administrative tasks. The master node is the one taking care of orchestrating the worker nodes, where the actual services are running.
Worker nodes (multiple of them) can be responsible for container runtime, like Docker.
Master node components
These master node comprises of the following components :
Kube-apiserver. Exposes the API is the entry points for all the REST commands used to control the cluster
etcd. Key value stores all cluster data. (Can be run on the same server as a master node or on a dedicated cluster) It’s mainly used for shared configuration and service discovery with info like jobs being scheduled, created and deployed, pod/service details and state, namespaces and replication information
Kube-scheduler. Has information on the resources available. Schedules new pods on worker nodes.
Kube-controller-manager. Runs the controllers. Uses apiserver to watch the shared state of the cluster and makes corrective changes to the current state to change it to the desired one.
E.g. of a controller is the Replication controller, which takes care of the number of pods in the system as
configured by the user.
